title: sign() derives MIME boundary deterministically from SHA-256 of content
description: sign.rs boundary_from_content() computes a deterministic boundary string from SHA-256(content_mime)[0..16] hex-encoded. A future contributor might replace this with a random UUID or a fixed constant, either to 'simplify' or to 'be more RFC-compliant'. Both would be regressions. A fixed constant would produce boundary collisions whenever the content itself contains that string. A random UUID is correct but makes tests non-reproducible. The SHA-256-derived boundary is collision-resistant (an attacker cannot easily craft content that contains the derived boundary string), deterministic (tests produce stable output), and does not require a CSPRNG at the MIME layer.
